title: CRLR/447/2018 of ASHISH KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME DEHRADUN

paras.text:
CRLR No. 447 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Manish Lohani, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. Rajendra Arya, Advocate for
respondent no. 2.
The provisions of Section 125(4) of
Cr.P.C. contemplates that a wife, who is living in
adultery, or a wife, who is living separately from
her husband, without any reasons or refuses to
discharge her matrimonial obligations, she would
not be entitled to receive any maintenance under
Section 125 of Cr.P.C., which is inclusive of final
maintenance as well as the interim maintenance.
Section 125(4) of Cr.P.C. is quoted hereunder:
"No Wife shall be entitled to receive an
allowance from her husband under this
section if she is living in adultery, or if,
without any sufficient reason, she refuses to
live with her husband, or if they are living
separately by mutual consent."
In the present case the impugned order,
which has been put to challenge by the revisionist,
is the order dated 17.04.2018 as passed by the
Family Court, Haridwar, in Criminal
Miscellaneous Case No. 293 of 2017 'Smt. Sheela
Das vs. Ashish Kumar' under Section 125
Cr.P.C., wherein, the Family Court by the
impugned order has granted an interim
maintenance while exercising the powers under
sub-section (2) of Section 125 of Cr.P.C. at the
rate of Rs. 4,000/- per month to the respondent no.
2, i.e. the wife, and at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- each
to the respondent nos. 2 and 3.
It has come on record that at the time when
the proceedings under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
itself was pending consideration, there had been a
corresponding proceeding, which was initiated by
the revisionist (husband) by invoking the
provisions contained under Section 9 of the Hindu
Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights,
that was also pending consideration.
On the previous occasion the learned
counsel for the revisionist was directed to provide
the information as to what is the present status of
the proceedings under Section 9 of the Hindu
Marriage Act, which was initiated by the
revisionist (husband).

Today, he has placed before this Court the
certified copy of the judgment dated 24.08.2019
as rendered by the learned Judge, Family Court,
Udham Singh Nagar, wherein, the learned Family
Court, after recording a finding that though notice
was sent to the respondent herein on her address
specified, but she has not put in appearance,
consequently, a paper publication was made on
21.12.2018 and despite of it when she has not
appeared, the proceedings under Section 9 was
drawn exparte against her and by the judgment
dated 03.04.2019, and ultimately the same has
been decreed exparte on 04.05.2019 in favour of
the revisionist directing respondent no. 2 to join
her matrimonial home and to discharge her
matrimonial obligations, this judgment so far
stands good.
It is a settled law that in those cases where
there is a decree of restitution of conjugal rights
and despite of the decree, where the wife has been
directed to join her matrimonial home and
discharge her matrimonial obligations and if she
does not joint back then she will not be entitled
for the grant of any maintenance either by way of
a permanent maintenance or an interim
maintenance in the proceedings under Section 125
of Cr.P.C.
Consequently, as far as the determination
of maintenance made by the learned Family Court
by its impugned order dated 17.04.2018 while
deciding the interim maintenance application
paper no. 8A, that is partly quashed so far it
relates to the determination of maintenance made
in favour of respondent no. 2 of the present
revision.
But, as far as the interim maintenance
determined for revisionist nos. 3 and 4 is
concerned, the said part of the order is maintained
and affirmed, revisionist is directed to pay the
same by 10th of each month.
Consequently, the revision succeeds partly
only to the effect with regards to the
determination of interim maintenance directed to
be made payable to respondent no. 2.
